verdict: Caution: lend selectively to ship-repair and small-vessel fabricators with tight covenants; avoid large shipbuilding order-book bets in Vasco-Margao until local demand data is collected.
title: Vasco-Margao Shipbuilding & Repair: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Shipbuilding and repair converts steel, labour and dry-dock time into cash, but the two halves behave like different businesses.** Repair is short-cycle: a vessel arrives, is docked, worked on and released within weeks, so cash comes back fast and margins are set by dock availability and urgency. Newbuild is the opposite: steel and labour go out for years before a hull is delivered and paid. **So when a proposal lands, first ask what share of revenue is repair versus newbuild; if newbuild dominates, ask for the delivery schedule and milestone billing terms.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Peer results show repair is the better-margin business.** Cochin Shipyard's Q1FY26 ship-repair revenue grew 157.2% YoY to Rs 629.6 crore while shipbuilding fell 16.7% to Rs 439 crore, and EBITDA margin held at 22.6% on the richer repair mix [1]. The same peer now guides FY27 EBITDA margin to around 14% from 24% in FY26, with shipbuilding at 10%-12% and repair at 22%-24% [2][3]. **So when a proposal lands, check the segment mix; if the borrower is mostly newbuild, ask what protects margin when the cycle turns.**

## What has changed now
**National output is strong but the local signal is weak.** India-wide IIP for NIC 30 is +25.3% YoY and +22.7% Apr-to-date [D], yet Goa GST collections are -1.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% and electricity demand +6.7% against India +9.5% [D]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's order book is Goa-based or outside; if Goa-based, ask for the last six months of billing to confirm activity.** The sources say little about Vasco-Margao specifically, so lean on first principles and the Cochin peer.

## Where to grow safely
**Pursue repair yards and small-vessel fabricators with visible dock utilisation and milestone billing.** Structure limits against work-in-progress, take monthly stock and receivable statements, and covenant a minimum repair-revenue share. **Avoid pure newbuild borrowers with long gestation and no milestone cash.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for repair-revenue share falling below the covenant, WIP ageing beyond the delivery schedule, and GST billing trailing the order book.** Any of these means stop and re-price.
